title: Local Hilbert--Samuel presentations and their admissible transforms
statement:
Let $X$ be a reduced scheme of finite type over $\mathbf Q$, locally closed in a smooth scheme $Z$ [def-pc-reduced-scheme] [def-weil-finite-type-morphism] [def-weil-closed-immersion] [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms]. Put $h_x(n)=\operatorname{length}(\mathcal O_{X,x}/\mathfrak m_x^{n+1})$ [def-weil-pbc-module-length], $\Lambda f(n)=\sum_{i=0}^n f(i)$, and $H_X(x)=\Lambda^{\operatorname{trdeg}_{\mathbf Q}\kappa(x)}h_x$ [def-kun-transcendence-degree] [def-weil-residue-field]. Then $H_X$ has finite image locally, is upper semicontinuous for lexicographic order, and cannot increase under a blowup with smooth center on which $H_X$ is locally constant. There is no infinite strictly decreasing sequence of its values along admissible blowups of a fixed initial finite-dimensional $X$.

At each $a\in X$, after restriction and an etale neighbourhood [def-weil-etale-morphism], there are a smooth closed $N\hookrightarrow Z$, a coherent ideal $I\subset\mathcal O_N$ [pqf-def-coherent], and $b\ge1$, such that $\{x\in N:\operatorname{ord}_x I\ge b\}$ is the local $H_X(a)$ equality stratum. Here $\operatorname{ord}_x I=\sup\{q:I_x\subset\mathfrak m_x^q\}$, allowing infinity for zero. A presentation means more than equality of these sets: along every finite admissible test sequence, its cosupport is exactly the locus retaining that Hilbert--Samuel level (with the level summed after a line product).

The test operations are smooth blowups with centers in that stratum having normal crossings with the ordered exceptional divisors, products with an affine line, and blowups of intersections of two exceptional divisors. Normal crossings means that the center is a coordinate subspace in an etale coordinate system in which boundary components are distinct coordinate hyperplanes. For an admissible blowup, $X$ and $N$ take scheme-theoretic strict transform and $I$ takes total transform divided by the $b$th power of the new exceptional ideal [def-nagata-global-blowup] [def-nagata-strict-transform]. For the other two operations take ordinary pullbacks of $X,N,I$; a line product appends the zero section as last boundary component. Blowups retain the ordered strict transforms of boundary components and append the new exceptional divisor. The ordered boundary of a test sequence is empty at the stage where the presentation is taken and consists only of the divisors created by the operations of that sequence (new exceptional divisors and line zero sections); exceptional divisors created before that stage are recorded history data and are not used as test boundary. Presentations are equivalent when all these test sequences agree.

At a singular point of $X$, use a minimal smooth local envelope (the ambient cotangent space maps isomorphically to that of $X$); a presentation is then etale-locally equivalent to one on the whole envelope ($N=Z$) whose ideal has order exactly its positive marking $b$ throughout cosupport. Presentations at regular points still exist; no finite maximal-order assertion is made for the zero ideal on a codimension-zero regular germ. Up to common etale comparison, the class of a presentation at a specified Hilbert--Samuel level is independent of the chosen minimal envelope and of its coefficient data. Along admissible histories it depends only on the intrinsic transformed scheme, the retained level and the ordered earlier center ideals, with the induced boundary data. It commutes with restriction and local smooth pullback: for a smooth map of relative dimension $r$ the level $H$ is replaced by $\Lambda^r H$, so equality strata and test conditions pull back. This does not assert that the numerical value of $H$ is invariant under a positive-dimensional smooth map. Emptying the cosupport of a presentation of a maximum stratum removes that maximum from the strict transform. These assertions concern presentations and their transforms, not a completed resolution tower.

source.place: ILO VIII 2.3.11--2.3.13, pp.93--94; detailed input WANTED: BMT arXiv:0905.3580 sections 6.1--6.3 and BM marked presentations. No Stacks tag states this presentation theorem.

proof.text: Apply [lem-trf-jet-level-topology-reachable-dcc] on affine charts: its finite jet presentations give local finiteness and lexicographic upper semicontinuity. Its reachable diagram bound applies to all finite admissible histories from the fixed initial scheme, including subsequences separated by plateaus; hence there is no infinite strict descent.

source.place: ILO VIII 2.3.11--2.3.13; BM/BMT assembly; re-split of old proof steps 1,2 and DCC part of 9

proof.text: After shrinking about $a$ using step 1, [lem-trf-regular-hilbert-coefficient-data] supplies the regular coefficients and positive weights. Apply [lem-trf-common-power-hilbert-marking] to form $I=\sum(c_{i\gamma}^{b/(d_i-|\gamma|)})$ on its smooth $N$, with $(I,b)=(0,1)$ for an empty list. This gives the initial equality locus, coherence, the controlled transform $e^{-b}\sigma^*I$, and nonincrease for every smooth locally $H$-constant center, including outside it.

source.place: ILO VIII 2.3.11--2.3.13; BM/BMT assembly; re-split of old proof steps 3,4

proof.text: Apply [lem-trf-coefficient-test-sequence-propagation] to these same coefficient data. Its prefix identity identifies transformed cosupport with the retained level after every finite test, with one summation per line product. The boundary starts empty and remains transverse to $N$; its ordered transforms and next centers therefore agree. This is the required presentation. Its smooth-pullback assertion gives the level $\Lambda^r H$, equality strata and tests on each relative-dimension piece, including restriction.

source.place: ILO VIII 2.3.11--2.3.13; BM/BMT assembly; re-split of old proof steps 5,7

proof.text: Choose a minimal envelope and apply the construction of steps 2--3 there. [lem-trf-minimal-envelope-coefficient-comparison] supplies such envelopes, positive essential transverse rank at a singular point, and the explicit suspension ideal $(z_1^b,\ldots,z_r^b)+p^*I$ of order exactly $b$. It also compares coefficient choices and minimal envelopes, retaining the ordered earlier-center ideals and induced boundary through admissible histories. Its regular zero-ideal case supplies presentations without a finite-order claim.

source.place: ILO VIII 2.3.11--2.3.13; BM/BMT assembly; re-split of old proof steps 6,8

proof.text: For a maximum level $H_0$, step 3 identifies its final equality locus with the transformed cosupport. If that cosupport is empty, equality is impossible; nonincrease from step 2 excludes values above $H_0$, so all final values are smaller. The reachable descending-chain condition of step 1 rules out infinitely many strict drops. All of these conclusions concern the stated transforms and tests; no resolution tower is constructed.

lean.note: The previous function_no_infinite_drops quantified over consecutive single blowups and only forbade a strict drop at every successive stage. It did not supply the node's descending-chain condition after passing to a subsequence separated by plateaus, as required by the dimension-profile proof step 14. The new module publicly imports HilbertSamuelLocalPresentations, retaining every existing numerical and marked-presentation declaration, and adds function_no_infinite_reachable_drops for levels attained after arbitrary finite admissible histories from one fixed initial scheme. Relation.ReflTransGen uses exactly the existing BlowupTransition; it includes zero blowups and supplies the source's fixed-ambient-dimension descending-chain assertion without introducing an arbitrary transition map.
